title: Particles explained
summary: A review of the logical particles as a detective agency: が, を, に, へ and で each answer one question about the event.

blocks.text: **Logical particles** say how the parts of a sentence fit together: who did it, to what, where, with what. Each attaches to a **noun** and the pair stays together. Think of them as a team of detectives, each asking one question about the event. **は** is not on the team: it only flags the topic.

blocks.title: The detective agency
rows: Who did it? / what is it?
What was the action done to?
Where is it / where does it go?
Where did it happen? / by what means?

blocks.text: **が** is needed in every sentence, even when it is hidden. It is also the only logical particle that works in a **description** (A is B); the others work with action verbs. And a logical particle never changes its job.
You can **be** in a park (に), but to **do something** there you need で. で also marks the **means**: the bus you go by, or the language you speak in.

blocks.en: (I) go to the park by bus.
(I) speak Japanese. (Japanese is the thing spoken)
(I) speak in Japanese. (Japanese is the means)

blocks.jp: さくらとメアリーが歩いていた。

items: **が** doer · **を** done-to · **に** target / place · **へ** direction · **で** place of action and means.
**と** joins nouns and says nothing about the action.
Do not confuse the particles and they will not confuse you.

questions.note: で marks where an action takes place.
で marks the means.

questions.prompt: （私が）フォーク＿＿ご飯を食べる。
questions.note: で marks what you use.

questions.prompt: 友達＿＿一緒に映画を見た。
questions.note: と says together with whom.
questions.en: (I) watched a movie together with a friend.

questions.note: で marks the language as a means.
に marks the target of putting.
questions.en: (I) put a book on the desk.

questions.prompt: 姉が町＿＿買い物をしている。
questions.note: で marks where the shopping happens.
questions.en: My older sister is shopping in town.

questions.instruction: Which particle answers 'where did it happen?'
questions.note: で is the place of an action.
と joins nouns.

questions.instruction: Which particle is NOT a logical particle?
questions.note: は only flags the topic.

questions.instruction: Which particle works in a description (A is B)?
questions.note: Only が works when there is no action.

questions.instruction: Which particle marks 'being in a place'?
questions.note: Being in a place is a target already reached.
バスで, 日本語で.

questions.prompt: に marks where an action takes place.
questions.note: That is で; に marks where something is.
で marks what you ride.
questions.en: I go to school by bicycle.

questions.instruction: Tap the place of the action
questions.note: で marks where the working happens.
questions.en: My older brother works at a shop.

questions.note: と says who goes along.
questions.en: (I) go to the park with my younger brother.

questions.note: に marks where the friend came to.
questions.en: A friend came to the station.

questions.note: Place of action: で.

questions.prompt: (I) go to the station by taxi.
questions.note: Means で, destination に.
questions.en: (I) go to the station by taxi.

questions.note: と joins the two nouns.

questions.prompt: (I) am studying in the library with a friend.
questions.note: と, then place で, then the verb.
questions.en: (I) am studying in the library with a friend.
